details:
I was experimenting with a simple c# script to assign shapekeys to be driven by bone rotations with customizable smoothing, and honestly, it works a treat in Unity and looks great, essentially opening up a whole new world of possibilities.

Sadly the only realistic workaround to getting that to work in vrchat would likely be a mass amount of ContactSenders/Receivers which are timeconsuming to set up and generally overkill for such a simple function.

Since you guys have already implemented vrc specific constraints, it doesn't seem like too far of a stretch to make such a component uploadable and usable in vr. 

You could even expand upon it by adding options for split axis drivers, which in all honesty could revolutionize the deformations of for example clothing. Currently, there is a well known and almost unavoidable issue with baggy clothing for vrchat avatars due to the distance of the weighted parts and the pivot point of the joints (armpits especially).

For a while now I have been utilizing contact receivers and senders to drive corrective shapekeys to bypass this issue, but they are far from perfect, takes ages to set up, and are locked to 1 shapekey per joint (realistically). With a split axis shapekey driver you could essentially have 3 or even 4 corrective shapekeys to ensure good and unique deformation without the previously mentioned issues.

Some examples of use-cases for such a component could be the following:

- Driving shapekeys for tendons on hands

- Driving rotation based corrective shapekeys on problem-prone meshes like baggy clothes

- Driving physically accurate shapekeys for cloth folds and the like.

- Driving knee / elbow / shoulder / spine compression shapekeys

- Driving any sort of shapekey for visualizing a twisting object

And probably many other use-cases

[Edit because I forgot to mention it, In terms of performance it shouldn't have much of an impact I think, there are already so many other systems or implementations that do mass shapekey transforms at this point that I don't see how this could be any worse, also, perhaps even better would be to expose it to a float or other parameter type instead of just a shapekey, as that opens up tons of other ways to use something like this.]
title: [VRCSDK] Addition of a simple bone-rotation driven shapekey driver system
